title: Weather Versus Climate Explorer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: View one temperature record at three time windows - a week, a year, thirty years - with the trend line refusing to appear until the window is wide enough to justify it.

learningObjectives: Distinguish short-term variation from long-term trend within the same dataset.
Explain why a single unusual reading does not establish a trend.

keyQuestions: How long a record do you need before the word "climate" is honest?
A record-breaking hot day is reported on the news. What does it prove?
Why is it important that the y-axis stays the same in all three views?
commonMisconceptions: Treating a cold week as evidence against long-term warming.
Confusing the seasonal cycle with a trend.
Believing a single record day shifts the climate normal.
assessmentOpportunities: Explains why a trend cannot be fitted to seven days.
Distinguishes the seasonal cycle from a long-term trend.
States that one extreme day is evidence of weather, not of climate.
